stem:
Madhav asks what integer $q$ satisfies $(-8)\times q = 56$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $q = -7$, because $(-8)\times(-7) = 56$ and unlike signs for $56$ and $-8$ make $q$ negative.
$q = 7$, from $56\div 8$, with the sign pattern omitted.
$q = (-8)\div 56$, treating the dividend as the missing factor run backwards.
$q = 448$, from multiplying $56$ by $8$ instead of dividing.

teacher.key_rationale: Missing-factor view: (-8)×q=56 so q=56÷(-8)=-7. Dropping the sign, reversing dividend/divisor roles, or multiplying instead of dividing all miss the integer-division hinge.
